editions.title: Last week on E-Grid
editions.intro: A busy weekend across three championships, with Formula 1, MotoGP and NASCAR Cup Series all racing on Sunday 11 October. Here is what happened around the world of motorsport this week.

items.headline: Singapore Grand Prix
items.detail: Marina Bay Street Circuit, Singapore · Sun 11 Oct
items.body: Max Verstappen won the Singapore Grand Prix from pole, seven point three seconds clear of Charles Leclerc, with Andrea Kimi Antonelli taking the final step for Mercedes. The result extended Antonelli's championship lead over George Russell from 84 to 102 points. Dry and hot at Marina Bay, with virtual safety cars on laps eight and thirty-nine.
facts: Max Verstappen won from pole, 7.3 seconds ahead of Charles Leclerc
Biggest climbers: Isack Hadjar from 22nd to 10th and George Russell from 19th to 9th
Fastest lap: Charles Leclerc, 1:35.202
Did not finish: Alexander Albon, Lance Stroll, Franco Colapinto and Gabriel Bortoleto
Andrea Kimi Antonelli's championship lead over George Russell went from 84 to 102 points over the weekend
Virtual safety car on laps 8 and 39

items.headline: Grand Prix of Indonesia
items.detail: Pertamina Mandalika Circuit, Indonesia · Sun 11 Oct
items.body: Marco Bezzecchi won the Grand Prix of Indonesia by four point three seconds from Raul Fernandez, with Jorge Martin finishing third for Aprilia Racing. He set a new lap record of one minute twenty-nine point nine six zero at Mandalika. Saturday's sprint had been won by Marc Marquez before Toprak Razgatlioglu, Jack Miller, Francesco Bagnaia and Fermin Aldeguer all failed to finish.
facts: Marco Bezzecchi won by 4.3 seconds from Raul Fernandez
Did not finish: Toprak Razgatlioglu, Jack Miller, Francesco Bagnaia and Fermin Aldeguer
Marco Bezzecchi set a new lap record, 1:29.960
Dry, 29°C air and 62°C track
Saturday's sprint was won by Marc Marquez

items.headline: Bank of America 400
items.body: Chase Briscoe won the Bank of America 400 from second on the grid by just zero point zero two nine seconds over Christopher Bell, with Ryan Blaney third for Team Penske. The victory moved him up to fourth in the Chase. Kyle Larson led most laps and holds a growing lead over Denny Hamlin, now forty-nine points wide with four races remaining.
facts: Chase Briscoe won from 2nd on the grid
Most laps led: Kyle Larson (97)
Stage winners: Stage 1 Kyle Larson, Stage 2 Christopher Bell
Margin of victory: 0.029 s
Kyle Larson's Chase lead over Denny Hamlin went from 40 to 49 points this weekend, with 4 races to go
The win lifted Chase Briscoe from 6th to 4th in the Chase

editions.intro: Formula 1 and MotoGP both had their winners decided this weekend in Singapore and Indonesia, with championship standings shifting across both grids. NASCAR's Charlotte round is still to come on Sunday evening.

lastRaces.headline: Rally Italia Sardegna
lastRaces.body: World Rally Championship's Rally Italia Sardegna came around Alghero in Italy on Sunday 4 October, forming round 13 of the season. It was another demanding test across Sardinia for the leading crews as they pressed on through the latter half of the calendar.

lastRaces.headline: Midwest Nationals
lastRaces.detail: World Wide Technology Raceway, Illinois · Sun 4 Oct
lastRaces.body: The NHRA Drag Racing season reached the Midwest Nationals at World Wide Technology Raceway in Illinois on Sunday 4 October. Top drag racers lined up for a key round of the championship on the Illinois strip.

lastRaces.headline: Motul Petit Le Mans
lastRaces.detail: Michelin Raceway Road Atlanta · Sat 3 Oct
lastRaces.body: IMSA's SportsCar Championship reaches its finale with the Motul Petit Le Mans at Michelin Raceway Road Atlanta on Saturday 3 October. The endurance marathon has long stood as the series' crowning event, capping another demanding season of sports car racing.

lastRaces.headline: 6 Hours of Fuji
lastRaces.body: The World Endurance Championship turned to Fuji Speedway in Japan on Sunday 27 September for the 6 Hours of Fuji. The circuit's steep climb past the summit has again defined this round, testing drivers and machines across a full endurance distance.

lastRaces.headline: Baku
lastRaces.detail: Baku City Circuit, Azerbaijan · Sun 27 Sep
lastRaces.body: Formula 2 brought its sprint and feature races to the Baku City Circuit in Azerbaijan on Sunday 27 September. The narrow street track threading the old city's walls offered another tight, technical test for the feeder series.

lastRaces.headline: Spa-Francorchamps
lastRaces.detail: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps, Belgium · Sat 19 Sep
lastRaces.body: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps has hosted racing since 1921, its 7.004 km lap threading through 19 corners. The series' fifth round came here on Saturday 19 September.
facts: 7.004 km lap, 19 corners, first raced 1921

lastRaces.headline: Madrid
lastRaces.body: Formula 3's tenth round came to Madrid, Spain on Sunday 13 September. The championship's Spanish round brought its racing to the city that weekend.

lastRaces.headline: Monza (double-header)
lastRaces.detail: Autodromo Nazionale Monza, Italy · Sun 6 Sep
lastRaces.body: Autodromo Nazionale Monza has hosted racing since 1922, its 5.793 km lap threading through 11 corners. The Porsche Supercup's seventh round ran here on Sunday 6 September as a double-header in Italy.
facts: 5.793 km lap, 11 corners, first raced 1922

lastRaces.headline: Season Finale
lastRaces.detail: WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca · Sun 6 Sep
lastRaces.body: IndyCar's season finale reached WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca on Sunday 6 September. As the championship's final round of the year, it brought the season to a close at the venue.

lastRaces.headline: London E-Prix
lastRaces.body: Taylor Barnard won in London for DS Penske, completing a Mahindra Racing one-two as Nyck De Vries took second and Edoardo Mortara third. The result leaves Pascal Wehrlein five points clear at the top of the championship, ahead of Jake Dennis.
facts: Pascal Wehrlein leads the championship by 5 points from Jake Dennis
